back: A tube full of liquid that carries liquid over a barrier to a lower level without a pump.
Tube full of liquid; outlet below the liquid surface in the upper container; bend less than about 10 m above that surface (for water).
Atmospheric pressure on the upper liquid surface; the taller outlet arm makes the pressure at the bend greater on the inlet side.
Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is passed on equally throughout it; liquids are almost incompressible.

front: Force on the large piston of a hydraulic system
back: F₂ = F₁ × A₂ ÷ A₁ (from F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂). The large piston moves A₁/A₂ as far.
Pedal → master cylinder piston → brake fluid passes pressure → wider wheel cylinder pistons → pads on discs → friction slows wheels.

front: Why does air in brake fluid make brakes spongy?
back: Air is compressible, so the pressure squashes the air instead of moving the wheel pistons.
Piston valve closed, inlet valve open: atmospheric pressure pushes water into the barrel; water above the piston is lifted out of the spout.
Inlet valve closed, piston valve open: water passes through the piston to the space above it.
Push: washer seals, air compressed, tyre valve opens when barrel pressure > tyre pressure. Pull: tyre valve closes, air enters past the flexible washer.

front: Maximum lift of a lift pump
back: About 10 m of water at sea level (h = p ÷ ρg), less at high altitude.
